requirements.scope_note: Sume dæge is a time expression, “one day”; sume is the instrumental form. Hwæthwugu means “something”; swilces is neuter genitive, “of this kind.” Ūte means “outside.”

requirements.scope_note: Ciricean is the source genitive or dative spelling corresponding to productive cirican: genitive when dependent on roof or window, dative after tō or locative in. The same noun can name either the community church or Chad’s oratory; context and Cook’s note distinguish the buildings.

requirements.description: gelōmlice; āna; in bēcrǣdinge / in gebedum geornfull
requirements.scope_note: Gelōmlice means “often”; āna, “alone.” Bēcrǣdinge means “reading books”; gebedum is dative plural, “prayers”; geornfull here means “occupied” or “intent.” In governs the dative in these expressions.

requirements.description: gehīerde; sęmninga; swā-swā; ęft æfter ðon
requirements.scope_note: Gehīerde is prefixed “heard.” Sęmninga means “suddenly”; swā-swā, “just as”; ęft, “again” or “afterwards” as the context requires. Æfter ðon means “after that”; ðon is the source dative demonstrative variant.

requirements.description: swētestan / fægerestan stefne; singendra and blissiendra; oð; āstīgan
requirements.scope_note: Stefne is accusative feminine singular, “voice.” Fægerestan means “most beautiful,” agreeing with stefne. Singendra and blissiendra are genitive plural participles used substantivally, “of people singing and rejoicing.” Oð means “as far as.” Āstīgan here means “descend.”

requirements.description: Ðā stefne and ðone sang … gehīerde
requirements.scope_note: The initial accusative objects belong with the later gehīerde inside the reported clause. Cwæð introduces the report. Ǣrest means “first.” Do not turn the fronted accusatives into subjects.

requirements.scope_note: Ēastsūðdǣle means “southeastern part”; hēanesse, “height”; winterlican, “winter,” agrees with genitive sunnan; ūpganges means “rising.” Ðanan means “from there.”

requirements.scope_note: Styccemǣlum means “little by little.” Nēalǣcton is third plural: the voice and song approached. Oð-ðæt means “until.” Becōm means “arrived”; the following singular reference is explained by Cook’s note 9a.

requirements.scope_note: Ðæcean is dative singular, “roof.” The relative ðe is governed by the later in, “in which”; the preposition follows its relative.

requirements.scope_note: Ingangende is a present participle, “entering.” Eall is accusative neuter singular, “everything.” Gefylde means “filled.” In ymbhwyrfte means “all around”; ymbsealde means “surrounded.” These continue the description of the song.

requirements.scope_note: Geornlice means “attentively.” Mōd is “mind”; āðęnede is “directed/stretched.” The whole attention expression means to direct one’s mind or attention to something; in has the accusative here.

requirements.scope_note: Here swā-swā means “about,” not “just as.” Healfre tīde is genitive, “of half an hour”; fæce is dative of the interval after which the event occurs. The hour sense of tīde is supplied separately.

requirements.description: ūpāstīgan; blissesang; ðȳ ilcan wege; unasęcgendre swētnesse; ęfthweorfan
requirements.scope_note: Ūpāstīgan means “rise up”; blissesang, “song of joy.” Ðȳ ilcan wege is the supported route expression, “by the same way”; ǣr means “previously.” Unasęcgendre swētnesse means “with indescribable sweetness” after mid. requirements.description: wunode; sum fæc tīde; wundriende and wafiende
requirements.scope_note: Wunode means “remained”; ðǣr, “there.” Sum fæc tīde is an accusative duration expression, “for a while.” Wundriende and wafiende are uninflected participles describing the observer as wondering and amazed.

requirements.description: mid behygdigum mōde; ðōhte and smēade; hwæt … bēon sceolden
requirements.scope_note: Behygdigum mōde means “with an attentive mind.” Ðōhte and smēade mean “thought” and “pondered.” The embedded question asks what the things might be or mean; sceolden is preterite subjunctive plural, with infinitive bēon.

requirements.description: ontȳnde; ēagðȳrel; handa; slōg tācen; swā-swā; gewuna
requirements.scope_note: Ontȳnde means “opened.” Handa is the source dative form of hand. Slōg tācen means “made a signal,” literally “struck a sign.” Swā-swā means “just as.” Gewuna means “custom” or “habit.”

requirements.description: gif hwilc mann … wǣre; ðæt … ēode; in; sōna
requirements.scope_note: Hwilc mann here means “anyone.” Wǣre is preterite subjunctive in the habitual condition. The ðæt clause states the content or purpose of the signal. In is the adverb “in”; sōna means “immediately.”

requirements.description: Cwæð … him tō; Gang; hāt; ēac swilce mid wes
requirements.scope_note: The separated him … tō identifies the person addressed. Gang means “go” (singular imperative); hraðe, “quickly.” Hāt is singular “command/tell,” with an accusative subject and infinitive. Hider means “hither/here.” Ēac swilce means “also”; mid is adverbial “with them”; wes is singular “be.”
